newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW - BT says Concert to break even.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - BT says Concert to break even.

text.p: British Telecommunications Plc confirmed on Thursday that its Concert Communications corporate networking venture with its American partner MCI Communications Corp would break even this financial year.

BT's finance director Robert Brace told Reuters in an interview that the business was "clearly ahead" of its two main rivals, Global One and Unisource, and had built up a $1.5 billion backlog of orders.
"We've got a backlog of orders of $1.5 billion, the customers love it, it's growing fast," he said. "It's the start of big improved services for multinationals around the world..."
Brace declined to detail figures, saying the company was coy because it did not want competitors to know any data. But he said current turnover was in the high hundreds of millions of dollars.

Concert boasts business from more than 3,500 customers in 41 countries. Contracts run between one and five years, but typically three, and newspapers say this indicates annual revenues of at least $500 million.
Concert faces competition from Global One, the trans-atlantic grouping formed by Sprint Corp, France Telecom and Deutsche Telekom AG, and WorldPartners, the AT&T -led consortium.
BT plans to cement the venture by merging with MCI this autumn, if it wins U.S. regulatory approval, to create a new company called Concert Plc.
